coverageGaps: The reported 168-unit planning count has not been reconciled to a named, versioned inventory.
No authoritative waterbody geometry or complete municipal/city crosswalk is validated; the reviewed national catchment dataset is planning context only.
Coastal, estuarine and brackish study-area identities remain incomplete.
Aurora, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Tarlac and Zambales require additional source-reviewed fish records beyond the named leads.
Regional species coverage, historical/current distinctions, taxonomy, locality precision, rights and safety information remain incomplete.
The NFRDI Meycauayan report supplies historical interview-based fishery names, not a present-day tributary-level fish survey or absence record.
The newly reviewed 2009 fish-name excerpts are aggregate across study sites; per-site tables, field dates, coordinates and item-specific reuse approval remain pending.

The 2025 North Luzon barcode paper spans Aurora, Cagayan and Zambales. Four GenBank endpoint records were spot-checked and expose only country-level location, not province or waterbody; supplementary rows remain held under the article's CC BY-NC-ND license.

The BFAR Bulacan profile adds 22 communal/inland waterbody name leads but no per-waterbody fish roster or geometry; Angat EMB monitoring station references are water-quality locations, not fish evidence, and report dates/methods remain unverified. The author-uploaded Angat preprint describes a Marungko visit and reports catches since 2005 from interviews; the visit date and voucher remain unknown. A later secondary table relabels 2005 as introduction year, so it is not used as a verified introduction or observation date.

The 2025 PSA QIFS Bulacan series adds province-level inland catch-production categories, but not site-resolved species observations. Its individual values were read from an independent mirror and only aggregate totals match the rounded PSA annual report; verify category values directly with OpenSTAT before any public use.

A bounded GBIF screen returned no exact Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus match for Bulacan, but zero exact-string results are not an absence finding. Its sole genus-level Bulacan hit has a Valenzuela/NCR source locality that conflicts with GBIF's Bulacan administrative lookup; PSA PSGC lists Coloong under Valenzuela, so it is excluded from Bulacan evidence.

A 12-row GBIF no-coordinate preserved-specimen screen surfaced three CC0 Smithsonian species records with the same February 1982 Malolos fish-trap locality on Manila Bay's northern shore. These are historical specimen assertions without map points; one same-locality genus-only row and eight other records were not projected.

A July 2018 DOTr/JICA-hosted railway EIS reports local-interview fish and other aquatic-animal catch categories for five freshwater ecology stations, including Labangan River in Calumpit, Pampanga River in Apalit, Malalam River and Masaluso in Minalin, and Calutcut Creek in San Fernando. The February field dates belong to environmental survey stations, not individual fish captures. The source mixes species-name spellings, genus/family identifications and broad local-name categories; rights and specimen identities remain unverified. No station coordinate is projected as a fish point, and no app assertion or safety claim is added.

nextStep.action: Continue Central Luzon source discovery with locality-resolved Bulacan freshwater studies. The bounded GBIF screen found one historical Quingoa River CAS specimen and zero exact GBIF waterBody-field matches for the 22 BFAR communal/inland names; neither result establishes current presence or absence, and the coordinate is too uncertain to map. Use the BFAR profile's 22 features as a discovery checklist only, not a fish roster; expand beyond the GBIF Perciformes filter. The 2022 EMB RSOBER report indexes three Angat River water-quality stations, but its full methods and sample dates were inaccessible, so do not infer current safety or fish presence. The author-uploaded Angat preprint reports an Angat-Marungko visit and interview-reported catches since 2005, but visit date, voucher and reuse are unresolved; do not treat this as a verified introduction year or current record. The separate 2014 proceedings remain unavailable and are not proven identical to the preprint. A separate 2015 Bustos Angat River Network study-name crosswalk agrees on four of six fish names; Trichogaster lalius has a taxonomic conflict and Misgurnus fossilis remains a voucher/spelling hold. No sample identities or sampling date were independently verified, and the study is not food-safety evidence. A 31-row corrected Actinopterygii screen also yielded one 1929 Angat Dam/Angat River CAS specimen assertion, prepared as historical text-locality evidence only. The separate no-coordinate Smithsonian screen prepared three 1982 Malolos fish-trap specimen assertions for Oxyurichthys microlepis, Drombus ocyurus and Butis koilomatodon; it has no coordinates, one genus-only row remains excluded, and these records do not establish current presence. Continue underlying Zambales/Aurora tables: Dibut's 22-versus-23 conflict and article reuse remain unresolved; the Masinloc-Oyon Bay FASPS report is login-gated. Agno ARB7 is one Paniqui station (10 taxa/137 sampled individuals) with wet/dry date mapping unresolved. Four GenBank spot checks were country-level only (four country-level GenBank checks); keep Cagayan in its own rollout phase, preserve separate Bataan river rows with no independent identity verification, and continue distinct river, lake, reservoir, wetland, brackish and coastal leads. Do not mark Central Luzon complete. The 2017 Meycauayan/Obando household study and 2022 UPLB thesis abstract add aquaculture and food-system context only; pond-culture or market fish are not wild river records. The 2025 PSA QIFS profile now has 38 direct OpenSTAT rows for Bulacan (34 catch categories: 23 numeric and 11 explicitly unavailable); available category values match the independent mirror within 0.015 metric ton after quarter rounding. Keep them as province-level statistical context only and never assign them to named waterbodies or current species presence. Seek recent, taxon-resolved Bulacan wild-capture surveys with dates, exact localities, methods and taxonomic support.
nextStep.currentFollowUp: Cabiao's six fish-name candidates now have a six-name Catalog of Fishes crosswalk; the two source spelling issues are resolved only at nomenclature level. Voucher/specimen identities, site names/coordinates and article-specific reuse permission remain unresolved. Keep the study research-only. Continue site-resolved evidence across remaining Central Luzon rivers, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands and coastal/brackish waters; pursue legitimate access to the Angeles 2005 thesis. The GBIF station-window zeroes and wider rectangle do not establish absence or site presence. Keep Central Luzon incomplete.
